config_name: Steam Deck LCD — Custom AMD 'Aerith' Zen 2 8-core / 8 RDNA1 CUs, 8GB LPDDR5-5500, 512GB NVMe, 7" 1280x800 60Hz IPS

specs.ports: 1x USB-C 3.1 Gen1 (DP alt-mode, PD), microSD UHS-I, 3.5mm
specs.keyboard_notes: no keyboard; on-screen keyboard in SteamOS/Desktop mode
specs.os: SteamOS 3 (Arch Linux + KDE Plasma desktop mode)

battery.notes: 40Wh, 7nm APU; identical to 256GB LCD. Engadget measured Hades 2h42m on an early LCD unit.

price.store: Best Buy CA / Amazon CA (stock clearance)
price.notes: Discontinued tier sold down at retail; LIST.md estimate C$1,249. Note: near the verified C$1,349 OLED 512GB price, so only a value pick when discounted.

reviews.quote: The original model was great, but this latest iteration demonstrates that Valve can improve on perfection.
One of the downsides of the first Steam Deck was its short battery life, which maxed out at eight hours, and that was only under ideal conditions.

praises: 512GB NVMe (faster than the 64GB eMMC original) holds several AAA games without touching the slow microSD slot
Same SteamOS console UX, controls and library as the OLED — verified/verified labels, sleep/resume, desktop mode
Clearance pricing often lands it well under C$1,000 at Best Buy/Amazon, making it the budget SteamOS pick
Standard M.2 2230 SSD and Valve's parts store keep it repairable and upgradable for a decade
For emulators and pre-UE5 libraries the performance gap vs OLED is zero — same APU architecture
complaints: Discontinued — stock is thin and clearance prices sometimes exceed sensible levels vs the C$1,349 OLED 512GB
Battery tops out ~4-6h light, ~2.5-4h gaming; Engadget measured 2h42m in Hades
400-nit glossy 60Hz LCD: no HDR, visible backlight bleed in dark scenes, poor outdoor readability
Runs warmer than the OLED in the same hands-on comparison; older fan is audibly louder under load
Wi-Fi 5 only and BT 5.0 — slower downloads and worse simultaneous Bluetooth audio + Wi-Fi behaviour

design_philosophy: The launch 2022 Steam Deck's previous top LCD tier, now a clearance SKU. It embodies Valve's original thesis — an open Linux PC disguised as a handheld console — at the largest LCD storage config; today it only makes sense at clearance discounts given how close LCD and OLED pricing have converged.
rating_notes: Ratings inferred from OLED 512GB anchor via SHARED-steam-deck.md LCD deltas (screen_quality −3.0, readability_dark −2.0, readability_bright −1.5, battery −1.0, thermals_noise −1.0, portability −0.5, productivity −0.5 for 8GB). Identical to the 256GB LCD except storage tier (SSD was NVMe on both 256GB and 512GB). Pro anchor: Tom's Guide original Deck review (4/5) + Engadget LCD comparisons.
